items.title: Mcbee interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2020
items.q: Scotty LaFaro was one of the greatest legends of all time but you could rarely find him swinging

ctx.x: Excuse me, that’s exactly what it is. I’ve got three young bass players that I’m teaching now and my profession entirely, given their youth, their time of development, is how, is number one how you fashion your quarter note. Your quarter note should be, once chosen, should be realized, that once it’s placed on the beat it should be exact, followed by another exact tone, given the quality of the rhythm at the time. You are the timekeeper. You’re the conductor. You are the vibe of the entire group. If that quarter…

young man now who is, I told him the other day I said, “Look you’re 19 years of age, at my time you’re way more advanced than me.” I mean this young man is like on the level of Scotty LaFaro, that kind of thing. But he had — he has until recently maintained a bit of confusion about his performances because he had no understanding of how to swing. You know? So I told him, I said, “Look, Scotty LaFaro was one of the greatest legends of all time but you could rarely find him swinging and playing a series of tones…
